newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Some Russian MinFins rise on U.S. durables fall.
newsitem.headline: Some Russian MinFins rise on U.S. durables fall.

text.p: Some tranches of Russian MinFin bonds edged up on Wednesday on a drop in the U.S. durable goods orders index, dealers said.
"The market was slow," said a dealer from Aljba-Alliance bank. "Only in the evening, when the U.S. released durable goods index was there any buying interest."

Orders for costly manufactured goods dropped 1.7 percent in December, the U.S. Commerce Department said on Wednesday. U.S. economists, who had predicted 1.2 percent drop in a Reuters survey, said the data should help the bond market.
The dealer said there was most growth in the third tranche and moderate growth in the fourth, sixth and seventh tranches.
The fifth tranche, seen by dealers as the most unstable, remained almost unchanged, she said.
President Boris Yeltsin's appearance on television late on Tuesday failed to move the market, the dealer said.
"We felt some optimism, but the market did not react in any way," she said. "We still view Yeltsin's health as a negative factor, preventing MinFins from rising like other Bradys."
But another dealer said that buying could snowball and the market could rise strongly. He said the fourth and fifth tranches could rise to 60.00 and 42.00 respectively.
